title: I Tracked the Porch-Pirate Ring Light Through Three Camera Apps

parts.text: I watched a gloved hand take my box at 11:42 a.m. on my doorbell app. The face was a ring light in a hoodie. I was twenty-nine, WFH, holding a shipping alert. I posted the clip in the block group. A neighbor said their cheap camera had a side angle. I did not go outside. The thief walked toward the alley like they knew the dead zones. Then my other neighbor's floodlight cam pinged motion at the same second with a better chin.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: A second app just caught the chin the ring light was hiding.

social.video_title: Doorbell clip, hoodie ring light, alley dead zone — Part 1/3
social.description: WFH, shipping alert, block group. Side angle incoming. Would you have opened the door?

parts.text: I collected three clips: mine, the side angle, the floodlight chin. The same pink shoelace in all three. I filed a portal report with the police non-emergency upload, not Facebook comments. A third camera, a garage one I did not know existed, emailed me because I was on the shared HOA alert list. It showed the thief getting into a car with a cracked taillight. I added clip four at 12:10.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Clip four has a cracked taillight and the HOA list is awake.

social.video_title: Pink shoelace through three apps, then a garage fourth — Part 2/3
social.description: Portal upload, not comments. Taillight. Would you have confronted the car?

parts.text: They recovered the box from a car that matched. The person was a delivery driver from a different app taking lunch with other people's tape. I got the kettle that had been inside. The block group learned to email portals. Ring lights are not invisibility. Pink laces are a fingerprint. I still WFH. I still wait for the chime. Four clips are a sentence. I did not need to be a hero in the alley. I needed apps to talk, and for once they did.

social.description: Different-app driver, portal, laces. Was a ring light a mask?
